notes.title: Announce new game: Railborn
notes.content:
Friends! We need to talk. Sit down with me. 

Parkasaurus was our first game as a new studio, and will always be #1 in our hearts. This especially means the community and all the encouragement and support we received. While we plan to return to the Parkasaurus universe - in the meantime we have been working on a new game. This new game may seem very different from Parkasaurus - but is actually born from it!

Our new game is Railborn and we'd love for you and your friends you to give us a Wishlist. <3

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2340970/Railborn

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/e9b9b491486fd3a4fb16d78e51cbbbd741467c56.png

How are these games related you ask? Let me tell you! We brought all our care and love for biomes and the environment from Parkasaurus over to Railborn. Collecting plants, building out railcars to have the perfect balance for each biome will be a major aspect of the game. There is more, but I don't want to bore you with all the similarities yet.

Railborn is a fresh new adventure for us. As you probably know Washbear is a 2 person studio - and we make games for passion, and this is what our hearts were calling. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/72dd631b7ddb4eb3b85540b91e9655728506b5df.gif

So how you can help us our? You know what I'm going to ask: 

Please - Wishlist Railborn, and then copy that Steam link above and paste it to your friends asking them to checkout the game and Wishlist.

Friends – Update 2.0 Sea Monsters is upcoming. I thought to discuss what everyone will see. Just a reminder:

Water Toys

Hats
I suppose our logic about Water Toys also applies to Hats. Real talk – I find the 6 new hats so freakingly hilarious on the Theropods I had to make them available to all. If this game isn’t about the joys of life then what is ya know?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/4fccc75d8a7a7ac605c2c65ae60ab2267a5dccb0.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/93db0a97f5085530eb1ee3f72eeecea14510de93.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/f5e002537c41eb35837c1b797bc559d280cb8e28.png


Experimental Controller support
Finally! For those who like to lounge back and play Parkasaurus with a controller, now you can. Why do we call it “experimental”? Wellll, because there might be a few hiccups still. The cursor now becomes center screen locked which makes building and movement in the game much easier. In fact, I find myself faster in a lot of aspects of the game when using the controller
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/4b5f83f8f3291a227bd9a83ef21074bc34886944.png


Quality of Life
A few notable quality of life additions in this Sea Monsters update:

UI goes to 125%
Yes – we were aware for quite a while the UI could be difficult for some people to read. I just wanted to make a quick note here; if increasing UI size was easy we of course would have done it a long time ago. The reality is that for a game like ours, increasing UI is a really tough feature; languages break, UI breaks, and this requires weeks of testing on our part. Of course, we love our community and you’re all worth it! Just that there are only two of us so we sometimes can’t fix everything, or fix it right away.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/6f8c3c5be7ee02a290e2593aefaf23aaf118bc17.gif

Reduced GPU Usage when V-Sync is off
You either get this or you don’t. For most players this was a non-factor, but for the few that had V-Sync off the game really put stress on your poor machines. Fixed!

Max people park 300 to 600
We had limited the number of guests in the park mainly because the game came to a crashing halt performance-wise if we went above the 300 number Well, we overhauled the animation system of our guests so everyone gets into the park. This very well might break the game in a way we have not thought of soooo.. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/7215959fe75d5ad6118ea39bf08b61866a25726f.png

Improved Performance
Remember when Parkasaurus became available on the Switch? (we are available on the Switch!). Well, we opened the hood of the game and cleaned up our wires a little which resulted in a nice performance boost for PC. Enjoy!


DLC Available
Of course - there also is DLC available here that introduces aquatic exhibits and sea monsters. More about this later this week. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/6efdb440a575a022bf410560d6ce9c058ec000f6.png

Oh and one awesome reminder: Click to Wishlist our DLC!. See you Thursday.


xoxo

notes.title: Update #56: Nintendo Switch & PC
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/94a86b82132c05b036ce229fa6fd58e2daf7f3e0.png

Big news friends! Parkasaurus is coming to the Nintendo Switch early 2022! 
Bringing Parkasaurus over was a challenge the two of us had always wanted to do ourselves. Playing the game on the Switch feels pretty fantastic – and I don’t think anyone else would have given the same love to the port as we did. Wait wait wait, so how does this relate to the PC/Steam version? Well, the controller support required for the Switch (a TON of work) is coming to Steam, along with some other cool tidbits I thought to talk about:



 Fence helper 
 Guest skeleton optimization
 Multi-threading NavMesh
 Controller Support



Fence helper
In the video, one can see two fence helpers. The blue bar that appears showing how the wall aligns is currently in the game. We now added a floating tile that helps the player not lose track of the cursor location. This makes creating fences with a controller or mouse snappier and quicker. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/485f445f7dad5d7084610c3a987bb0b6a780a4dd.gif


Guest skeleton optimization
Who knew the skeleton in the models of the guests took up so much computing power! Maybe some of you knew. Each guest had an entire animation skeleton that the game had to keep track of. Multiply this by 200, 300 guests, and that is a lot of wasted CPU! Now all our skeletal animation was converted to vertex animation so the GPU could help out. This means more guests on screen, which also means we can raise (or remove) the guest cap. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/a1002c72012a4bf4ea4031b5ccbf321b5e73f870.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/8cc40cb42b07358a08b97e8c4301bd3f5477f481.png


Multi-threading NavMesh
We’ve improved the rebuilding that occurs every time an object is placed in Parkasaurus. The game is broken up into regions that get activated more or less depending on the point of view of the player. This results in a much snappier and lag-free experience building the perfect park.

Controller Support
Everyone said controller support was a lot of work. Did we listen? NO! Was it a lot of work? YES!
Adding controller support to us meant more than just being able to play Parkasaurus with a controller – we wanted the experience to feel as good if not better than keyboard + mouse. We underestimated how complex the interactions are between all our UI windows that have to be solved with a controller. The video below looks simple, but we had to decide and work on the ordering opening/closing windows. Phew.

Update

 Dinosaur Tycoon
 New Dinosaurs
 New Fences
 Campaign Missions now in Custom Mode

 Dinosaur Tycoon
Dinosaur Tycoon is a new challenge mode that has been added to the game. Dinosaur Tycoon requires you to achieve a Park Appeal of 50000 and have 300 guests. The game in this mode is also much more difficult, with higher prices for supplies and the needs of your dinosaurs being more demanding. There is an achievement associated with this challenge. You can find this mode in the Customize section, under the Mode dropdown.
 https://i.imgur.com/64oTTwSl.png

 New Dinosaurs
The Parkasaurus dino family has just become bigger! Each dino family in the game now has a new dinosaur joining the team. New dinos added to the game include:

 Diplodocus
 Euoplocephalus
 Coelophysis
 Pachycephalosaurus
 Sinoceratops
 Hesperosaurus

Realistic Mode
Believe it or not, some players are not in love with our derpy dinos. For them – we have now added a  REALISTIC toggle on the front menu to change your dinosaurs into a more “realistic” texture. (sorry, no feathers!) (This is just an OPTION, not default) Check out these good looking dinos:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/929a283b8131ab89da0421b0a7f6948eda7ee408.jpg

Dinosaur Variety

Hello! This week let me tell you about updates to what we call Dinosaur Variety. A player should be rewarded for having a greater variety of dino tiers within their park. Let’ s explore this idea.

Currently in Parkasaurus there are 4 tiers of dinos: Imperfect, Uncommon, Rare and Epic. Now the Info pane on your guests reveals the Dinosaur Variety experienced by your guest in addition to the total number of dinosaur seen. If a guest has seen too many dinosaurs of a certain tier they become bored, and donate less. 

https://i.imgur.com/CdGeIWWl.jpg

In the picture above the guest has seen 1 Uncommon dino, 2 Rare dino, and 1 Epic dino. No boredom!
A guest will donate proportional to the Appeal of your dinosaurs which increase with tier. This is Dinosaur Variety experienced by a guest at a raptor exhibit: 

https://media.giphy.com/media/SYdcM7GgxUfTpo9mPp/giphy.gif

This exhibit contains 1 Velociraptor and 2 Oviraptor. The guest donates the full amount for each dinosaur. You will notice that a guest grows bored quicker for lower-tier dinos.

We indicate boredom has set in with red bars as opposed to green:

https://media.giphy.com/media/f3uanUbwPkUfNwysQi/giphy.gif

A guest still donates when viewing a dinosaur of a tier they have become bored with but at a greatly reduced. 

Moral of the story: Be sure to keep Dinosaur Variety!

Also, this is a picture of the raptor exhibit from above. Apparently the Oviraptors decided to attack the lone Velociraptor.

https://i.imgur.com/aLunWuIl.jpg

notes.title: Update #43: Info Booths
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/c4d699ad4dbc67fbb00bdb3aeac88715c89f2c79.jpg

Info Booths

Hi friends. Today I’d like to talk about changes and improvements upcoming with Info Booths. Our objective with Info Booths is to provide players with a way to help direct guests deeper into their park. Just like you and me, when a guest arrives at a park they often will stop to look at the first dinos. As your park expands you eventually have cooler dinos with high appeal farther from the entrance. It is helpful to direct your guests to these new dinos.

 https://i.imgur.com/XsCBXxNl.jpg

How do Info Booths work? 

First, place your booth. You now have decisions:

 Placing Beacon
 Choosing Attraction

To help illustrate the functionality of the Info Booth look at the park heat map below.

https://i.imgur.com/5AZpkgY.jpg

Notice that not many guests have journeyed to the top of the park. Also, notice the farthest exhibit has only received $272 in donations. Not a great situation if my highest appeal dinos are in this farthest exhibit.

Let’s move the Info Booth beacon to where we would like a guest to visit. 

https://media.giphy.com/media/Ig9vQm0e1y1nlZtqEU/giphy.gif

Second, let me select Fun as the attraction a guest will find. The three options are Food, Fun and Bathroom. Guests who are looking for Fun walk towards the suggested beacon.

https://i.imgur.com/cwD7Ez2.jpg

Now, look at the park heat map with our Info Booth helping. 

https://i.imgur.com/cPMWzqg.jpg

Notice that many more guests have explored the exhibit at the top of our park. Also, notice this donation has received $9405 in donations! Of course, this also means the park has received fewer donations at the exhibit closer to the entrance. The Info Booth also displays on the map how many guests used their service. Interesting decisions to be made.

And did I mention the upgraded Info Booth teleports guests to their destination? Well – they do! 

https://media.giphy.com/media/THBbPOiQsOTJGKkkCt/giphy.gif

notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/8dd22255eb95e87e1ca2abba3f3c37b80caaff68.jpg

Dino Food
Happy March! (whoah slow down 2020). Our upcoming patch has a few changes involving dinosaur food that I’d like to chat about. Our motivation was to provide players with a few different strategies when choosing how to feed their dinosaurs, both in ways to save money, and also ways to improve their dinos well being. 
 https://media.giphy.com/media/J4tCWwfiDk48q29ozI/giphy.gif 

 Food Specialties
 Food Slots
 Feeder Bonuses
 Translation Help - Localizor!
 PTR up this weekend


 Food Specialties
 https://i.imgur.com/p3eqsTSh.png 
Are you interested in saving a few dollars when feeding your dinosaurs? Now you can buy them food appropriate for their size. If your dinos happen to large, then buy food that is suited for large dinos. The benefit to this is foods specific to a dino size are much cheaper than the generic food. For example, Tree Leaves are half the price of generic Plants. 
 https://media.giphy.com/media/USUpfxZfAQ1F3ENEiX/giphy.gif 
Your total food inventory can now be found hovering over the Vegetarian and Meat icons.

 Food Slots
 https://media.giphy.com/media/ZZrBgCAZMVmvf6EdwS/giphy.gif 
You assign each feeder what food to be filled with through the feeder info pane. By default, feeders are assigned to be filled with the generic Vegetarian (Plant) or Meat food (Fresh Meat) that are suitable for all dinosaur sizes. Selecting a food specialty means your Veterinarian now fills the feeder with this food instead of the generic food.
Just be careful! Dinosaurs will ignore a food specialty not appropriate for their size. For example, above I have my Veterinarian filling the feeder with Grass that I know is suitable for small dinosaurs like my Minmi.

 Feeder Bonuses 
 https://i.imgur.com/pbDeYz7h.jpg 
Did you not all feeders are built equal? Feeders currently have two types of bonuses:

 Capacity: These feeders can hold more food so your Veterinarians do not need to return as often
 Health: These feeders provide a Health bonus every time used by a dinosaur.
The bonuses on the feeders can be found at the bottom of their descriptions.

notes.title: End of Day
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/b529f5b86a9852f0d055b82b6f38f9d6f6422762.jpg

End of Day
Since Parksaurus entered Early Access the most contentious aspect of the game has been how we handle the end of day. The two of us have always envisioned Parksaurus having a day-night cycle, this made sense to us since we wanted seasons, places for dinosaurs to sleep, and a more immersive feeling of the days in and out of the park. Our desire for players to have more connection with their dino best friends meant trying to ensure players felt the life cycle of their dinos, that you watched them grow each and every day. This was always our motivation for a day-night cycle. This also meant having an end of day.
After reading and listening to you, the players, we have heard your frustrations with the end of day. We are implementing a LOT of changes to improve the end of day experience. I’d like to chat about UPCOMING changes:

 Toggle option to go directly into the next day!
 Integrating the Finance Wrap-up screen into the computer overview
 Remembering camera position
 Remembering tool selection
 Bright end of day warning
 

Toggle go directly into the next day!
https://media.giphy.com/media/LODsID6hzq8votseue/giphy.gif
That’s right. When the end of day arrives a toggle option appears in the upper right portion of the screen. If the toggle is enabled your park will immediately go into a new day. Stock up on food and let the sim carry itself out. 😊
Integrating Finance Wrap-up into computer
https://i.imgur.com/HlWuzKH.png
The first time seeing the end of day finance screen is cool. After that, the finance screen becomes much less cool. It is an extra click, it takes away valuable time! In addition – we had always desired for your office computer to be an important tool, so naturally, it made sense to put the important financial screen front and center. 
Remembering camera position
https://media.giphy.com/media/f5dwTDWTwdbHWGAaS4/giphy.gif
Have you ever been trying to get the perfect picture of your favorite T-Rex in a Witch hat and the end of day ruined your shot? No more! We remember your camera position, mode, and angle when starting a new day.
Remembering tool selection
https://media.giphy.com/media/dt6KqWGasr0O8vvK6b/giphy.gif
I noticed my flow was often ruined by the end of day when building. I found myself trying to position the perfect fence length and BAM, end of day! Have no fear, your tool selection is now remembered when starting a new day.
Bright end of day warning
https://media.giphy.com/media/Sti5KWBR7n1zTFSnmF/giphy.gif
Some of you have experienced this, some have not. Basically players were getting startled out of their flow at the end of day. A bright warning has been added as you approach the end of day.

In conclusion – we heard your feedback. This is why Early Access is amazing. You, the players, have made Parkasaurus a much better game. While our solutions might not be perfect for you specifically, we try to get the best consensus possible. 

xoxo Taky & Smashlore

notes.title: Update #38: Tuning & Testing
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/e677ac1d77ef6b7205fb422449a4ad7dd81d6115.jpg

Tuning & Testing
This post is a little offbeat. I thought it might be interesting to see how Parksaurus has changed since entering Early Access. 

Every time a major tuning change is introduced into the game we run all-day simulations. Essentially this is for two reasons: 


 To see if the game tuning is having the desired effect
 To identify any unforeseen issues
 

Money
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/322c51d3e4b6c4805463c7d0e69d2acb1686d5f2.jpg
This graph shows how much money an “average” park made over the lifetime of the game so far. You can see when Parksaurus entered Early Access that money was pretty easy to make. In response to your feedback we started to tune this back, and then REALLY tuned this far back – seen as the sharp drop. Too far! With more tuning, we slightly increased the money generation and feel pretty happy where we are now.

Garbage
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/49bde369ce9ceca691c9c1e4ba4495a12d8512e6.jpg
I find this graph a cool example of how our simulation system identifies problems. This graph shows how much garbage an “average” park generated. You can see the sharp drop in the garbage after one of our simulations (shown with arrow). This led us to identify guests were not dropping garbage because they were getting stuck on the navigation mesh!

Waiting in Line
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/37802a2406a3388ab7ec2b6dbafccb9a85b73e07.jpg

This graph demonstrates the constant (any often unseen) optimizations we are always trying to implement into the game. This graph shows the time spent waiting in line on “average” for guests at the admission booth. That sharp drop occurred when we made a custom hybrid navigation system. This is how we verify improvements!

Poop
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31320585/41c8e5beea3d58d898831d3590a9f167071a0538.jpg
Finally, this graph shows how much poop dinos created on “average” over the lifetime of the game. Why did this increase as development went on? We actually have no idea. The dinos are living AI entities so who knows.

And, if you got this far, here is a little sneak peek a toy we’re currently working on, with many more to come!:

https://media.giphy.com/media/eKOUJ3YLrxoLLsTzxE/giphy.gif

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/75c3a179f149d5de7f2751476cdeef6ff5df7433.jpg 
Update #28: Analytics
Recently we’ve been getting mods support ready for Parkasaurus and hopefully will have a test version up on PTR this week.
A few people have asked us about a discount. Our response is that we feel the game is currently on a discount until more content (like a campaign, breeding, ++) is implemented and the price will slightly increase. We have no intention of putting the game on a discount until after 1.0; the main reason being our community who supports us in Early Access deserves the best-priced product for them taking the risk in believing in us. We don’t take that lightly. 
Blah blah blah, but what is this update about? Alright! Lot’s of background work:

Update:

 Mod Preview
 Analytics

Mod Preview
We’re aiming to have a mod enabled version of Parkasaurus up on PTR very soon. Currently you will be able to add Dinosaurs, People and Buildings. Implementing mods for the game has turned out to be more work than expected – hence you didn’t hear from us for a little while. Sorry about that!

  https://i.imgur.com/faJfbI4.jpg 

Today I was testing out some free assets from the Unity store and figured “Hey what about a ship that serves fish and chips?”. Right? Well just so happens they had a free ship. I added our custom building shader and wham bam we have a ship store in Parkasaurus. 
Of course, dinos and people are presenting more of a challenge. Still, we persevere for the community!

https://i.imgur.com/oldtnn5.gif

Now, to be clear, this is NOT the Parkasaurus style, and I find it quite hum drum… but, a “realistic” dino skin. (where are the feathers?)

https://media.giphy.com/media/cKPZzudoO5ffYXd7St/giphy.gif

Ok ok, I can maybe get a bit more on board for dino party skin. 

 https://i.imgur.com/bj8OuiH.jpg

Now, rocket launchers on an Achelousaurus? GROW UP.

 Analytics
This might be less interesting to some, and more interesting to others. Recently more time has been spent looking at the newer systems we’ve implemented in the game – for example maintaining the energy of your guests. If your guest’s energy goes to 0, they leave the park. Seen below, we started to examine, ”Ok, should I see a difference between a park with no benches (energy refillers) versus a park with benches. 

 https://i.imgur.com/jMDF4yK.jpg

The top graph shows a histogram of the number of dinos seen by guests depending on if the park as benches or not. The park without benches clearly has a lower distribution of maximum dinos seen, a huge portion maxing at 11. The park with benches has a distribution of higher seen dinos, most notably a lot of guests who saw 13 dinos, then 14, 15 and 16. Great! This indicates the benches are extending the time guests spend at the park by maintaining their energy above 0.
The bottom graph demonstrates the difference between guests who have a total park allotment time of 0.4 vs 0.8, 1.0 being a full day of time. Guests that have 0.4 total park time see no difference between a park with benches or without benches. This indicates to us the limiting factor is not guests running out of energy but rather running out of allocated park time. We will likely be tuning this a bit.

https://i.imgur.com/dTjxCIl.jpg

Here we decided to examine a few basic metrics to ensure we didn’t have issues with our guests going into idle too often. graph top-left Shows us the total amount donated by guest depending on the number of dinos they’ve seen. As you can expect, the more dinos seen the more guests donate. Of course, there seems to be a plateau around 12 that we’re looking into. Any ideas? graph top-right We were worried that guests were chilling (a random idle) too often, but see that the average donated by guests seems fairly consistent regardless of their chill totals. graph bottom-left We also were worried that doing non-dino activities (like shopping) was consuming too much a guest's allocated park time, and again this was not the case. graph bottom-rightFinally it was interesting to see the actual distribution of chills per guests during their visits. Some guests chilled 26 times? Talk about taking it easy. Anyway, from all of this we’re hoping to push the perk system into a more meaningful gameplay experience.

Dino Money & Items v0.620
Hello Parkasaurus friends! I’m happy to share with you some details of the Dino Money & Items Update (v0.620) that is currently live and what is coming up next. First, let’s chat about the major changes in v0.620.

Dino Money & Items v0.620

 Carnotaurus
 Hats!!!
 Doors
 Decoration System Overhaul
 Portal Overhaul
 Economy Balancing
 Guest Meters
 News moving forward
 
Carnotaurus
What can we say? There are already more Theropods in the game than any other dino family but the Call for the Carno (C4C) was too strong. Of course, getting your hands on a Carnotaurus is no easy feat in regular play. What will your adult Carno look like? And more importantly, what sort of sun protection will they have? Be sure to share with us.
 https://media.giphy.com/media/mCD17yUy9RoMloPHN7/giphy.gif

 Hats!!! 
SO MANY HATS. Here is the thing, you won’t find them in the store. What?! You need to get a shovel, and, some real cash flow, to dig into the depths of the Earth. New hats will only be available from Hat Treasure Boxes found when digging in the portal. Hopefully, someone out there will create an exhaustive list of the new hats added (hint: there are 12).
https://i.imgur.com/WRhzBuu.jpg

Doors 
Even we have to agree that only have 1 boring Wooden Door was getting old. Since you’re all a creative bunch we wanted to give you some options on cooler ways to let employees enter the exhibits. 
 https://media.giphy.com/media/l1TqOpdZT7fFeyXhKr/giphy.gif

Decoration System Overhaul
The present Decoration System in the game was not particularly interesting and truthfully was never given the time it deserved. Now strategically placing your decorations matter. Your guests enter your park with a value of 0 for their Decoration meter. This meter slowly fills as they are surrounded by your awesome park extras. How can you tell what your park decorations look like? Well, turn on the Decoration Heatmap View found on the bottom left. Note, Tier 2 decorations need to be researched and bought in order to max out your guest’s decoration meters. 
 https://media.giphy.com/media/chz0erAHgO1LvHqYtK/giphy.gif	

Portal Overhaul
The portal has received some love. A few highlights:

 Auto-Dig added (but at a price!) 
 Select how deep into the portal you’d like to go; the deeper the better rewards!
 Choose a portal team from a list of your employees
 Portal rewards – now find Hat Boxes, Science, and Hearts along with the original rewards!

 https://media.giphy.com/media/SqO0aI15Xa4k5aprG1/giphy.gif

 Economy Balancing
This no doubt will be a contentious change. But our community is so amazing I look forward to hearing their feedback. Remember when money was really easy to make? We’ve been analyzing data from our great PTR volunteers and now challenge you to the new balanced Parkasaurus Economy! For those of you less interested in having to balance the books and would rather focus on creativity – don’t worry you can still make a Customized game.
 https://i.imgur.com/Y3I8R0Sh.jpg

Guest Meters 
A more subtle change involves the guest meters. You’ll note that the energy meter has been pulled out of what contributes to your guest’s overall happiness. Now keeping your guests energized is an important aspect of keeping them in the park. By doing this we were able to remove the “decaying” that occurred with the remaining meters; something that was anxious inducing (for me) and also resulted in your guests draining their meters while walking to their cars at the end of the day – thereby lowering park scores & review stars. 
 https://i.imgur.com/IcgbBbSh.jpg

 News moving forward
Again – huge thanks to the early supporters and everyone who has written a Steam review for us. Next on the horizon:
 Mods (this features it 90% done, and we will be revealing more shortly)
 Bugs! Sometimes you might not hear from us for a little while, that’s because there are still a bunch of bugs in the game
 Price increase

I would like to talk briefly about a price increase. We’ve always felt it important to value the game at what we think it is worth. As we add more features the price of the game will likely go up a small amount to account for this. Also – we feel it a nice Thank You for early adopters. Now, we aren’t doing this today, but we want to give you a heads up long before this happens. 
Again, thanks to our amazing, amazing community.

notes.title: Update #26: House Cleaning
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/c4fc036c542a40c1cc57633314a5421f7beb9869.jpg

House Cleaning
Hello our Dino family! First – we hope everyone is doing healthy and well in this New Year. This is a quick Update, and truthfully, maybe unexciting for many of you. With that said we wanted to continue our transparency with the community. 

We decided to do a major pass on some of our worst offending bugs, and then do a first pass update on the economy before implementing Mods. Now, the technical work for Mods has been completed and ready to go; it just felt wrong bringing new players into a game that had gained quite a few bugs since release. The challenge of adding new features is that one usually adds more bugs. This Update is termed House Cleaning because that’s what we’re doing, cleaning/fixing up the Parkasaurus house before putting in an updated economy and Mods. 

We appreciated your amazing support and understanding during this recent bug fixing stage. On the outside, the bugs don’t look like much, but on the inside, they are a lot for the game! Here are a few of the more random bugs we fixed:

Update:

 Great view up here!
 This park is … dirty
 Kentro-Sharks


 Great view up here!
Turns out with the update to our custom Navigation system that the collisions within the roofs of many buildings was being seen as walkable terrain. This resulted in your employees thinking they could walk up high, and never being able to get down because of the elevation difference. Case in point:
 https://i.imgur.com/7jDkp6w.jpg

This park is … dirty 
We started getting reports of people’s parks being over-run with garbage. Well, that’s exactly what was happening. Our logic system for the janitors calculates all the tasks in their immediate surroundings, ranks them, and usually chooses one to do. This works most of the time. But there turned out to be a tipping point of garbage pieces (messy guests) where your janitor would become paralyzed with deciding what plastic wrapper or can to pick up. The result was them becoming confused and picking nothing up, leading to more garbage, leading to more confusion.
https://media.giphy.com/media/495ME2xgiaClEgRo0q/giphy.gif 

Kentro-Sharks 
Do you ever hate it when your Kentrosaurus become Kentro-Sharks? An elevation bug for our dino friends entered the game where nobody really knew where their feet belonged. This resulted in dinos walking too high (especially new born babies) and also way too low. I will admit the scales swimming around the park looked cool, but unfortunately not practical. 
https://i.imgur.com/qF0LmLT.jpg

To all you early supporters – thanks a ton. Don’t worry, we’re still thinking of something awesome to give everyone who has helped us in Early Access. Also, owning the game already means the price can never go up for you :)

notes.title: Parkasaurus Enters Early Access Today!
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/211a4a006eb3f4332f33b4712cdaf38ba728e401.png

Parkasaurus Enters Early Access Today!

Hi Dino friends! The time has come for Parkasaurus to enter Early Access. 

First off the two of us who make up the Parkasaurus team want to thank everyone who playtested, gave us feedback, told their friends or forums about us, or just hung out in Discord and was awesome. Thanks. This has been a scary adventure which all of you made much easier. Now we begin the next phase!

We hope the Parkasaurus family gets bigger today, and with that comes a new group of people to help choose the direction of where we go. Yes – the next few weeks will likely be fixing terrible bugs and game balancing, but it also will be an opportunity to hear feedback from everyone and update our roadmap. Early Access support is crucial for a 2 person team like ours, and, we can’t thank you enough.

Not to stray too far from our usual updates, I just wanted to provide a little background to Parkasaurus and then some fun stuff. 

The Origin of Parkasaurus
We thought it would be fun to share the origin of how we came to start making Parkasaurus. Although the game nods to previous games before it, the impetuous came from a handmade game design doc in the form of a colorful binder that is called DinoGame, with sparkles and all. DinoBook was split by tabs into categories, detailing how a dino tycoon sim game could work. Well – thanks to one of our wives, we fell in love with the idea of DinoGame and ran with it.
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/5f6e5799c47fb5bf9a5e3b8b0c1a7f976bedd75d.jpg

Now a little fun:

 Wandering your park at night
 No You Clean the Toilet
 Food Court Design
 Dinos with Style



 Wandering your park at night 
Spending the entire Parkasaurus day can sometimes be stressful, especially if you get a breakout. I like to take the time and use the free cam to enjoy the cool views at night.

	

 No You Clean the Toilet  
In Parkasaurus the employees automatically will try to find tasks to do around the park. You can toggle them to just do one task if you want (eg. There is a ton of garbage and you want your janitor on ultra clean-up duty). We also let you assign directly in game different tasks for your employees by using the right mouse button. 



 Food Court Design  
There is a lot of emphasis on Exhibit Design in Parkasaurus, and for good reason. Happy Dinos mean more money to expand your park. But it also is fun to take your time and plan how you’ll create little food courts around your park. 



 Dinos with Style  
Perhaps most importantly in Parkasaurus you’ll need to equip your dinos to look good. Your dino best friends won’t be able to wear accessories until they become adults; so that gives you plenty of time to research and stock up on the coolest items in town.



 Parkasaurus has arrived

Parkasaurus Update #020 : Steggos Coming Home

We sent our Steggos out into the wild and they’ve found their way back. That’s an analogy for life, and also an analogy for sending out the Parkasaurus tutorial for a little feedback playtesting. At the moment we’re heavily looking at the game after the tutorial, so days 7+ of in-world time. We see so many different directions Parkasaurus can take and look forward to having people help out with those decisions. 

And of course, as a reminder in 2 weeks, we’re releasing into Early Access on September 25th (eep!). Thanks to everyone who has been helping spread the news about Parkasaurus and getting our Wishlist numbers up! 

 Update 020 Topics 

 Expanding the Family
 Steggos Coming Home
 Watching the Hatch
 Valley o’ Dinos
 

 Expanding the Family  
The size requirements for each exhibit is dependent on the number of dinosaurs that are living there. If you add a new baby to your dino family you’ll need to increase the exhibit size to keep everyone happy. The easiest way to accomplish this is to add the extension fence first then remove the dividing portion (otherwise guests might get snacked on). The best part though is watching the baby & parent bonding at the end. :)
https://media.giphy.com/media/g07enZNl0fFvwmBFxa/giphy.gif

 Steggos Coming Home  
What can I say? Sometimes I find it fun to just create a massive Steggo herd to come storming out of the mountains onto our poor little food court village.
https://i.imgur.com/OuN185Z.png

 Watching the Hatch  
Although not necessary I like to make an elevated enclosure around a hatching dino egg – like this little Tric. Oh, and to place down a front row seat for a perfect view. I'm very excited to see what other ideas people come up with in the game.
https://media.giphy.com/media/4H5koyWLMlhP3yPNBJ/giphy.gif

 Valley o’ Dinos  
We have a random terrain generation tool for the game that we will likely include for Early Access but keep it as an experimental feature until we have more time to smooth out the kinks. If people really find this fun we also can start to integrate it more into the game. I find the feature really useful for creating fun scenes like my Valley o’ Dinos.

notes.title: Parkasaurus Update #018 : The Pursuit of Raptorness
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/c2225de4399458448f35a6f4db085463497b087d.png

Parkasaurus Update #018 : The Pursuit of Raptorness

Parkasaurus is humming right along. We’re feeling pretty happy with our complete re-do of the starting tutorial, and now are focusing on gameplay after 7+ days of park time. This includes income balancing which is a pretty big challenge at the moment, with only two of us it can be hard to get in a 2-hour game session. 😊 But! Have no fear, we know soon the community will be helping us out (hopefully) with balance, and providing great suggestions on what needs to change. We’ve already had some pretty cool suggestions on our Discord and Roadmap (all links below)

 Update 018 Topics

 See in the dark
 Pack Hunting
 Fence Fun
 Bonus: Experimental Terrain Generator


 See in the dark 
We added in some more interesting streetlights to give the player some more options when designing their park at night. My favorite is the string lights that attached from tall scenery objects in your park to other tall objects. This meant having to go through all our park build-ables and add the appropriate collisions which is a time-consuming process…but well worth it; I think. (I better of thought that since I had to do it)


 Pack Hunting 
In order to push our dino behavior a little farther, Velociraptors pack hunt when trying to attack a large dino in their exhibit. They intentionally try to walk through the tall grass before the attack (any dino in tall grass gets a reduction to their "view-ability" from a guest or other dinos. It might be fun for them to pack hunt guests also, perhaps I’ll try that next.


 Fence Fun 
Whipping up a bare-bones exhibit to test our new range of fence materials including an overhaul on icons, values, and imagery. Fence materials affect the viewability of the exhibit from the view point of the guests, and perhaps, more importantly, the strength of the fence. A stronger fence means less repair work for your janitors or allows you to keep in some pretty scary best dino friends.


 Bonus: Experimental Terrain Generator  
I’m still entertaining the idea of how and if we’ll include the random terrain generation on day one of Early Access. Either way, I’d love to get it into player hands and see what cool pics they can come up with.

Parkasaurus Update #016 : Ohhh behave – Dinosaur A.I.

Recently we’ve been working on how your dinos behave and co-exist with each other in the park. Our first step was to design how a single dino experiences the world by itself, and now we’re throwing all the dinos together. This results in a bunch of unexpected results. Luckily, we’ve implemented a utility AI that solves many of the problems and results in cool emergent gameplay.

 Update 016 Topics

 “Are you my mom?”
 Inter-species exhibits
 Dino mindfulness
 Camera fixes and don’t forget the fun


 “Are you my mom?” 
Turns out Milo the baby Triceratops was quick to accept Daisy as his mom. In Parkasaurus you now can have unconventional family structures; a newly hatched baby dino usually latches on to the first adult dino they meet; even if a different species.
https://i.imgur.com/Wnzssaw.png

 Inter-species exhibits  
Experimentation into inter species exhibits has resulted in many questions, for example, what if the species desire different biomes? Does this mean it is possible to have 2 biomes in a single exhibit? If so how does the system decide the amounts of a biome in an exhibit when more than one exists? .
https://media.giphy.com/media/9tVXOikV5Y8Jxi9FjD/giphy.gif

 Dino mindfulness

 Camera fixes and don’t forget the fun

Parkasaurus Update #015 : Everybody needs a little private time 

Lot’s to share for this Parkasaurus Update. In addition to improvements to the game, we’re also starting to tie in all the non-gameplay tasks that are really important like translations and reaching out to people who might be interested in previewing the game. There have been a few requests for a roadmap so I’d like to get that up for everybody sometime this week. Alright, let’s get to it:

 Update 015 Topics


 A Little Privacy Please
 Late Night Dino Gazing
 Employee Micro-managing
 Seasons are back in style!


 A Little Privacy Please 
Our continuing series that dives a little deeper into a few of the mechanics in Parkasaurus this week covers the Privacy System. This is one of the mechanics we think really makes Parkasaurus unique from the other dino park simulators and allows people who love to design a chance to be really creative with both form and function.
https://youtu.be/NTuts4BOnLE

 Late Night Dino Gazing 
As we start to get closer to an Early Access release we’ve been going back over some of our original features to figure out which ones we want available for day 1 EA, and which ones we need to receive additional feedback from the community about. The general consensus from our Discord channel has been night lights are awesome – so we had to do a little work to get our  night lights  functioning again with our new shader system. 
https://i.imgur.com/xpNkj14l.png

 Employee Micro-managing  
The employees in Parkasaurus automatically find appropriate tasks in the park to do based on a scoring system; this consists of distance to the tasks, dire need of the task to be done, assigned priority, etc. Sometimes though you might see an overflowing garbage can that you just need to get cleaned; so, we added the feature to directly assign tasks to your employees in the world. 
https://media.giphy.com/media/BoICgsGTTjnZ9BnNUG/giphy.gif

 Seasons are back in style! 
Autumn is here. Well, more is the case the two of us have been fixing free cam bugs. This includes inspecting all our seasons using the free cam. My favorite season currently in the game is autumn but I must say winter is right up there.

 Dinos just want to have fun
 Exhibit Lists
 Bonus: Park grand opening


 Employee waypoint updates 
In Parkasaurus your employees become vital once your park starts to grow, it is a great lesson in delegating out the work. We’ve been improving employee pathing; now you have 3 choices: 

 random - the employee wanders the park looking for tasks to do
 waypoints – you assign the route for an employee to follow
 proximity – you assign the employee to stay tethered to a certain area

https://i.imgur.com/UjkG9hxl.jpg

 Dinos just want to have fun
Toys! Toys! Toys! We’ve been finalizing the toy system and changing how this affects your Dino best friends. For example, some toys might improve the health of a Dino (eg. A vaccine is in the ice cube!) or sometimes toys are just for fun, and therefor increase the enrichment of your Dino.
https://i.imgur.com/DGMHiJEl.jpg

 Exhibit Lists 
There are many interesting systems in Parkasaurus that sometimes can be missed by players. Last week we added some much-needed info panes that we never realized were very important to have, for example, a list of Dino exhibits. It may seem intuitive to put this in but it's amazing what you just don't see when you’re in the thick of developing a best friend Dino tycoon game 😊
https://i.imgur.com/R2DHT2Fl.jpg

Hi there Parkasaurus Warriors! The next update has arrived. The game is tightening up; a few big features (that are hilarious to see in game) and more graphics updates. At Washbear we hope to be as transparent as possible, and want to let you know that we’re trying very hard to get you an Early Access date update. Thanks for understanding! Parkasaurus Update #009 : Party Hats

Alpha Version 3 current milestone…what is closer than close?
A very large update to the Parkasaurus privacy mechanic has been implemented over the last week. Now there are more options for deciding how to design your exhibit. As always the focus is on your dino best friends so a few more dino accessories were made thanks to our Discord vote.  Oh, and of course more food refilling options and dino poop!   

Update 009 Topics

Party Hats
What type of manager are you?
Privacy is Happy – but for who
Somebody has to clean it up…


 Party Hats 
Are accessories for your dino best friends the most important feature we should be working on? The answer is DEFINITELEY YES. Our Discord channel recently voted on what dino accessories they wanted to see more in Parkasaurus, and recent winners were Unicorn Hat (+2 enrichment), Cone of Shame (+1 health) and Hotdog Hat (+1 bonus to eating). Earn those science points to be sure you too can have a full assortment of accessories. 
https://i.imgur.com/G4aYmJU.jpg


What type of manager are you?
Your dino best friends are going to be really hungry, and we mean HUNGRY. Keeping your feeders refilled is a demanding task in Parkasaurus. The question is do you refill the feeders yourself by items from you inventory bag, or do you have your veterinarians do the work? Or a combination of both? Choices choices.
https://media.giphy.com/media/9XXO7d9ULr4uedfkt2/giphy.gif


Privacy is Happy – but for who 
Your privacy heatmap allows fine tuning of your dino exhibits to be a balance between what is best for your dinos, and what keeps your guests paying money! Obviously your dino best friends are paramount – so be sure to use tall grass, wisely shape your exhibits, and mindfully place your guest paths along the fences in such a way as to maintain a decent amount of privacy.
https://media.giphy.com/media/28kJl6PSoMZZZsDWav/giphy.gif

Sadly our dinosaurs lost the ability to poop – but luckily that was fixed! Part of raising your baby dinos into full adulthood is ensuring their exhibits are clean. Be sure to hire a veterinarian and a janitor to help out.

Hello Parkasaurus Warriors™! Sorry this is a few days late, blame Google and their faulty calendar. (I should be careful they hear everything). LET’S DO THIS. Here is your Parkasaurus Update #007 : Potpourri

Alpha Version 3 current milestone!
There is still a major focus on the core loop of Parkasaurus, this is really our #1 priority. In addition though, we’ve started to do a graphics improvement pass that is Early Access suitable (eek) – although Alpha 3 is still the current target. With all that said there are lots of interesting updates to choose from this week.
Update 007 Topics

Dino baby logic & integration
Graphics FX improvements
Achelousaurus is the big winner! (chicken dinner?)
Donation system!
Bonus: Privacy Heat Map extensions


 Dino baby logic & integration 
Last time we chatted you found out that we are indeed having Dino babies ready for Early Access. Since then we’ve created new baby models, figured out all the code bits so they grow over time into awesome adults, and implemented their baby brain logic. Here is a little Steg Baby hanging out with mom.
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/a4eee82e66cc9c6b76ea0c8bc9b4fef50d05e436.gif


 Graphics FX improvements 
We really want Parkasaurus to have a unique look – so there is an extra graphics pass being done on exhibit tiles and paths. In the picture you see the tiles sand, grass and mud. Each of these tiles forms the start of your exhibit design. Your tile type dictates what sort of biomes you can build into – but that really depends on your design choices. The tiles when placed down procedurally create what you’re seeing.
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/1708239d72a2356d793200189fde81cf1881c52a.jpg


 Achelousaurus is the big winner!
Achelousaurus was chosen as the winner from our most recent poll on Discord. Now the poll is deciding what Sauropod we should put in next.	
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/1a72e96c2000116ea5758c2d2b4737d78d6b94d5.jpg

 Donation system
We're experimenting with a new system that represents a guests donation potential with money bubbles above their head. As the guest builds up donation from seeing happy Dinos, bubbles appear representing the amount of donation, from 1 to 5. Happier Dinos means more money bubbles. The donation amount will dissipate over time until they reach donation boxes that are strategically place by the player.
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/cd16bb5ca01a899916662f9e3e393a3296a121e7.gif


 Privacy Heat Map extensions
More work on the privacy heat-map; adding vegetation toggle and implemented paths near the edge of exhibits reduce privacy. Exhibit shape and path placement is important!
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/e074393f81baa58a6a32ad482fcdcdddb9570622.gif


 Parkasaurus Warriors! 
Keep it up! We appreciate you SO MUCH for helping spread the word about Parkasaurus by sharing us via that cute little green button below, Wishlisting us, following us on  Twitter or posting about us on reddit or forums. Being a Parkasaurus Warrior is such a big help to us. Spread the word!

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/7e81db4aa1f22deae6a944b6a8b66dad25651b6f.png

Howdy Parkasaurus Warriors™. Apologies for this update being 1 day late; we were busy getting ready for the most romantic day of the year: February 15th - Galileo Day! The day when we celebrate our love of dinosaurs and all topics science. Here is your Parkasaurus Update #005. 

Alpha Version 2 – Closer still…
This was a very exciting week. Topics to chat about from least exciting to most: we created some cool shaders to give the plants and fauna more life,  developed robust management graphs for the in-game office computer and lastly started our first playtests with close friends. As you can imagine it was exciting and scary! One of our playtests ended when the water flooded the park…

Update 005 Topics

Plant Shaders
Management Analysis System
Playtests


Plant Shaders 
A core dimension for us when creating Parksaurus is to emphasize the importance of using appropriate fauna in your best friend Dino exhibits. This is why we strive to do everything we can to help make the worlds you design more beautiful. Our newest shader does just that; giving life -like wind motion to all the plants in the Parksaurus world, using a 2d noise map that moves across the world. The amount of wind varies with the time of day, time of year and the width & height of the plants. It looks great:

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/b33e38e0c4650140f4c216b77cea8813d9e8099a.gif

Management Analysis System
In Parksaurus you’ll have the chance to retire to your office to examine the park budget; where did you lose money? Which of your best friend Dinos generates the most money from the guests? Did curly fries sell more than waffles fries on Thursdays? Management graphs were put into the office computer so you can check revenue, profit, etc. throughout the days. 

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/cb9e94755e8d71938aeb71c51e876c57beeeb4b1.gif


Playtests
The first playtests occurred last week to much terror and excitement. Mostly terror? As predicted the playtests were … interesting. One always wants a raving success when the first people try out your game; the reality is usually tears. Luckily we’ve gone through enough playtests to know the roller coaster of emotions. Ok, joking aside we learned a lot. Our favourite game ending bug though was water leaking out of a Sauropod exhibit and slowly but surely flooding an entire park on Day 7. Good times:

Hello fellow Parkasaurus Warriors ™. Jeez we’re one month into 2018 already! No worries, I have your bi-weekly (or is that bi-monthly? Nobody knows) Parkasaurus update for you. 

Alpha Version 2 – Closer…
Schedule is back on track after a small setback last week. Our upcoming objective is: be able to play all the features of the game AND have them make sense. The catch is the 2nd part of that sentence “have them make sense”. Since we’re all making this game together – I’ll share with you that one of the toughest parts of making games is for people to understand what the heck the feature even is. This requires some internal UI testing that occurs next week. Exciting!

Update 004 Topics

Discord! 
Privacy 2nd Pass
Lighting Improvements and Shader Optimization
Dino Magic Items


Discord!
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/46788db19166f62d6ebb6a2ee1668a68e1b395f5.jpg

choose a Dino family to join (Stegosauria Swooners anyone?)
vote on what Dinos we make next
post or read about cool science articles



Privacy 2nd Pass

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/f83bd5b9437fa98578a04c1e1ffe1bdf36112b75.jpg

Privacy is an aspect of exhibit design. Depending on how you shape your exhibit, place the walk paths, and what enrichment items to install, changes the exhibit privacy profile - represented by a privacy heatmap. There are a lot of factors that go into this. And of course, your Dino behaviour is greatly affected by the privacy profile. With that said - we're doing a 2nd pass on the privacy mechanic to improve the clarity to the player (and to ourselves).


Lighting Improvements and Shader Optimization
This is a two-fer. 
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/2203c51db428e71d53ddb6435e3b0ecd9f47dc9f.gif

For example our fire shader – made from a combination of layered noise masks using 3d cylindrical meshes - was very cool, but caused serious performance issues. We applied a 2nd pass and now the fire is silky smooth.

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/3df510d5c6a5c3b4669b1c93dfec43be54e8aee0.jpg
Even better (it gets better!) was changing the color palette of the Parkasaurus world to match more closely to our vision, and to change the lighting curve from gamma to linear. And wowy – your park is going to look amazing.

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/3809534b9e79444fa4969318449d8d970caae3c6.jpg

Howdy Parkasaurus Warriors. 2018 has begun and both MT and I hope you’re doing great. One of us got the flu but has fully recovered. Alrighty, down to business.

Alpha Version 2
Everything looks to be on track. We might take an extra week to reach Alpha Ver 2 in order to give a thorough pass on Dino logic. Specifically carnivore behavior – we’re looking to make their demeanor more personable; ie. more like lions at the zoo as opposed to berserk monsters from the movies. (don’t worry, they still eat people)

 Update 003 Topics

Bio-Diversity 
Preview Tool
Upgrade Sets


Bio-Diversity
We’re hoping players create beautiful diverse exhibits for their Dinos that include a range of fauna and decoration. The earlier version of bio-diversity tried to reward players to achieve the perfect balance between trees : rocks : plants. After designing a few exhibits we quickly found this system stifled the creativity of players. Not cool!  Instead we reward players for bio-diversity, but don’t punish players if this is not their prime focus in Parkasaurus. Much better.  The bars shown in the image now indicate the amount of each fauna / decoration type in the selected exhibit, and also how many of level 1 types versus level 2 types. Level 2 exhibit type items are researched and give bonuses to Dino happiness among other cool benefits. 
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/e5b12c2cb5874717f9834612d856cd62e0f823ea.gif

This maybe isn’t the most exciting picture to show – but it is the most exciting for me to work with! We created a tool to create awesome preview pictures (right) for the in-game build menu based off the original 3D models (left). What this means for Parkasaurus  is 1) beautiful preview images 2) keeps us on pace to get the game into your hands.
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/e23244a109b296b539f9342f0b370fd8aaf000f2.png

For example, the admissions booth can be upgraded to Level 2, Level 3. Every upgrade comes with both a visual change AND an increase in park performance. The increase in performance depends on what is being upgraded, so in the case of the admissions booth you can imagine increased performance means serving customers quicker, and having additional booths to accept MORE customers (not shown).

notes.content:
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/7e81db4aa1f22deae6a944b6a8b66dad25651b6f.png
Hello Steam friends. 

I was hoping to start posting an update every few weeks to a) let everyone know what we’re up to b) let you know we’re still alive. Now – apologies if these posts are on the lean side – since there are only 2 of us on this game I might not spend as much time writing this as wish I could. Still, updating all of you is probably #1 on my “TODO” list so time will be found!

Alpha Version 2
MT and I have Alpha Version 2 (AV2) as our next major milestone. Basically this means we’ve put a hold on adding new features and going back through older features to make them more awesome. With that said I’m sure MT will ninja in a few features as we go along.

Update 001 Topics
A few select topics we worked on recently:

    Exhibit Privacy System
    Dynamic Water
    Dino Skins (Shader)


Exhibit Privacy System
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/087e82f7a724fe72016b61de3be94fb33c3b7de0.jpg
An important aspect of designing your Dino exhibit(s) is privacy. Your Dino friends are affected by privacy; now, some Dino species are more resilient to hoards of guests gawking at them; but all of your Dinos require some down time. How much privacy your exhibit has depends on the shape of your exhibit, materials used around and within your exhibit among other factors. In the picture above is an exhibit demonstrating privacy: the privacy toggle is on so you see a privacy heatmap within the exhibit showing what parts are private, and what parts are not private. Understandably areas near guest viewing areas (paths) are not private, so you can immediately see how you decide to design your exhibit directly impacts on your Dino’s privacy.

Dynamic Water
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/36f12c7789430f792f0001608d9fbdc8a28d1415.gif
We now have moving water! First it looks cool. :) More importantly though, water is an essential aspect of your exhibit. The amount of water in your exhibit transforms the type of biosphere thereby being more suitable for one type of Dino species versus another. Water also dictates what types of trees, plants & rocks you can successfully grow in your exhibit. 

 Dino Skins (Shader) 
We really want people to see each of their Dinos as unique and special. Therefor we made a cool shader (a shader is a special piece of programming code that does something specific with game graphics) that gives the skin of each Dino a unique look and color scheme. I probably linked the least cool of the results I’ve seen for far in the game, but it hopefully gives you an idea.

Thanks to all you early Parkasaurus Warriors
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31320585/b08c1f593114cd7cd85c806bc9ecae4042345d40.jpg
If you’re reading this, then you’ve decided to give some of your valuable time to a couple of devs following their dream – so thank you. We can use ALL the help we can get so please Wishlist us, follow us on Twitter or post about us when you can. Thanks!

Disclaimer: Any crazy features we write about might change by the Early Access version
